name: The Pale Fever
about: A fever nobody can name empties a lord's town street by street. You can shut the gates and let it starve, pay for physicians, or trust a hedge-woman's cure. If it reaches Kingsmere, you decide whether the King stays with his people or runs to a rival's hall.
title: The Pale Fever

new.name: Mother {first}
new.memory: I've seen this fever before, in the marsh villages, and I know what breaks it.

beats.speaker: warden
beats.text: In {sick} the dyers fall sick first, then the bakers. Their skin goes white as tallow, and they fall asleep and don't wake up. By the new moon the bells ring for the dead every morning.

court.text: {warden} of {warden.house}, grey from lack of sleep: "The fever's in {sick}, Your Grace. If I shut the gates, my people starve. If I don't, it leaves on the merchants' carts."

options.label: Shut {sick}'s gates until it burns out
options.hint: {warden.houseName} −15 · the fever stays put · the town goes hungry
options.result: Chains go across {sick}'s gates. Nobody goes in or out, and the bread runs low.

options.label: Send the royal physicians (150 gold)
options.hint: {warden.houseName} +10 · they might find a cure, or die trying
options.result: Three royal physicians ride for {sick} in beaked masks, with a cart of vinegar and myrrh.

options.label: Keep the roads open for trade
options.hint: costs nothing now · the fever spreads
options.result: The carts keep rolling out of {sick}, and some of the carters look pale.

beats.speaker: warden
beats.text: Behind {sick}'s chained gates the people eat the seed corn, then the dogs. Mothers lower their children from the walls on ropes and beg the guards to take them.

court.text: {warden}: "I kept the gates shut like you told me, Your Grace. Now the town has hunger as well as fever. Send bread, or let me open them."

options.label: Send grain over the walls (200 gold)
options.hint: {warden.houseName} +15 · the town lives long enough for a cure
options.result: The King's grain goes over {sick}'s walls in baskets. The ropes come back down with thank-yous tied to them.

options.label: Keep the gates shut
options.result: The gates stay shut. That night the guards hear singing behind them, then axes.

beats.speaker: warden
beats.text: The starving people of {sick} smash the chains with a smith's hammer and scatter down every road, and they take the fever with them.

beats.speaker: healer
beats.text: An old woman from the marshes walks into {sick} with willow bark, moss and a knife for bleeding. The first three people she treats wake up. The physicians call it witchcraft.

court.text: {rival} of {rival.house}: "A marsh witch is cutting your people open in {sick}, Your Grace, and calling it medicine. The septons want her burned, and so do I."

options.label: Put {healer} under your protection
options.result: A royal order hangs over {healer}'s door. She keeps working and asks for more moss.

options.label: Let the septons burn her

die.how: They burned me at {sick} for curing their children.

options.result: {healer} burns in the square at {sick}. The next morning the bells ring again.

beats.speaker: rival
beats.text: A cupbearer at Kingsmere goes white at the high table and collapses into the dishes. The Pale Fever is in the King's own hall.

court.text: {rival}, already on horseback: "Kingsmere is full of the dead, Your Grace. {refuge} is clean. Come with me tonight and rule from my hall until it passes."

options.label: Stay with your people
options.hint: the people love you for it · you might catch it
options.result: The King walks the sick streets of Kingsmere with a vinegar cloth over his face, and the city cries to see it.

options.label: Wall yourself up in the inner keep (300 gold)
options.hint: you're safe behind stone · the realm runs without you
options.result: The keep's doors are bricked up behind the King with a year of food. The realm only hears his voice through a grate.

options.label: Ride to {refuge} with {rival}
options.hint: {rival.houseName} +20 · the King is in a rival's hands
options.result: The King's household rides out of Kingsmere at midnight under {rival.house}'s banners.

beats.speaker: warden
beats.text: The King's hands are cold at council. By evening his cupbearer whispers that they've gone the colour of tallow.

court.text: {warden}, quietly, at the King's bedside: "You've caught it, Your Grace. We can fight it if we start tonight. If we wait, it won't wait for us."

options.label: Send for every physician in the realm (600 gold)
options.hint: the most expensive night of your reign · the fever might break
options.result: Physicians ride in from every house all night. By dawn the King's fever breaks, and the treasury is down the cost of a small war.

options.label: Let {warden}'s hedge-woman bleed the fever out
options.hint: {warden.houseName} +15 · the old ways, and you owe them
options.result: An old woman from {warden}'s lands bleeds the King and burns bitter herbs. He lives, and {warden} never lets the court forget who saved him.

options.label: Hide it and hold court as normal
options.hint: costs nothing · the fever doesn't care
options.result: The King sits on the throne in gloves and furs and talks about the harvest. Nobody dares look at his hands.

beats.speaker: rival
beats.text: The King wakes with tallow-white hands and never wakes again. Kingsmere rings its bells for nine days.

do.fall: The Pale Fever takes the King in his own bed. {rival} rides into a silent Kingsmere and is crowned before the bells stop ringing.

beats.speaker: rival
beats.text: At {refuge} the King's rooms are fine, but {rival.house}'s men guard the doors, and every letter he sends goes out with {rival}'s riders.

beats.speaker: rival
beats.text: {rival} announces that the King is too ill to rule, so {rival.he} will ride to Kingsmere and rule for him. The King's own guard is kept outside the gate at {refuge}.

beats.speaker: healer
beats.text: {healer}'s willow and moss go from town to town in the King's own carts. By the thaw the bells of {sick} only ring for weddings, and people name the fever after the King because he beat it.

beats.speaker: warden
beats.text: The Pale Fever burns itself out with the first frost. A third of {sick} lies in the lime pits outside its walls, and the crown that lived through it has aged for it.
